study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience) dataset; Single-site dataset from Aalto University (Kaltiainen and colleagues).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) [29]... We employed a dataset originally measured by Kaltiainen and colleagues [27,28], comprising resting-state MEG recordings from 25 mild traumatic injury patients and 20 healthy controls.

answer.SINGLE-SITE: patient and control for clinical research (test/validation sets for classifier)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Cam-CAN was used to build the normative models (Z-score statistics); The Aalto dataset (25 mTBI patients, 20 controls) was used to evaluate the classifier performance via nested cross-validation.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: A normative dataset comprising 621 healthy participants was used to determine the variation in power spectra... we trained support-vector-machine classifiers on the quantitative deviation maps for 25 mTBI patients and 20 controls not included in the normative dataset.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The full normative model used 621 healthy participants. The age-matched and random models used subsets; the age groups for evaluation were 18-67 years (sum of decade counts: 56+92+104+93+95 = 440).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: resulting in a set of 621 subjects. The number of subjects in each age group was 56, 92, 104, 93, 95, 102 and 79... The age groups were defined according to the normative dataset as 18–27, 28–37, 38–47, 48–57 and 58–67 years.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Italinna2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative dataset; Methods / Model training and validation

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: For the full model (n=621), the weighted mean age was calculated using the counts and midpoints of the seven age decades (18-87). The age-matched model used five decades ranging from 18 to 67 years.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: nearly 700 healthy participants aged 18 to 87... The number of subjects in each age group was 56, 92, 104, 93, 95, 102 and 79... (18–27, 28–37, 38–47, 48–57, 58–67, 68–77 and 78–87 years)

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The Cam-CAN dataset is described as containing approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade. For the total of 621 subjects, a 50/50 split is inferred.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: contains measurements from approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade
